item.dc:creator: Tyler Brooks
item.description: They say the best camera is the one you have on you, and the same goes for cars — no matter what you need to do, you're probably best served by the car you already have rather than jumping through hoops to swap it out.

They say the best camera is the one you have on you, and the same goes for cars — no matter what you need to do, you're probably best served by the car you already have rather than jumping through hoops to swap it out. But, sometimes, even we automotive adventurers are forced to concede: We simply have the wrong tool for the job.

Now, because we're automotive adventurers, that's not likely to stop us. We're often going to just use the wrong vehicle for the wrong purpose, and so earlier this week I asked you all for your best tales of doing just that . Today, we look through your answers, many of which had to do with driving incredibly unsuited cars on unsuitable tires through deep snow and ice. Godspeed, you beautiful fellow Northerners. As a former daily driver of a Scion FR-S through upstate New York lake effect snow, I feel an instant camaraderie with you.

Recovering materials from end-of-life batteries is a key means to secure much needed critical minerals (CRMs) resiliently and sustainably. With increased recycling, Europe can reduce imports of CRMs, in turn reducing external dependencies. However, Europe’s battery recycling industry is struggling to scale, with over half of Europe’s battery recycling capacity currently at risk . The Circular Economy Act must introduce measures to help scale Europe’s battery recycling capacity.

item.title: Mazda Comes To Its Senses, Cancels Misfit CX-70, Replacing It With Two-Or-Three-Row CX-90s For 2027
item.dc:creator: Chloe Adams
item.description: The automotive industry raised a collective eyebrow a few years back when Mazda announced that it would sell a two-row version of its excellent three-row CX-90 , but as a new model under the new name of CX-70 , and for good reason.
item.content:encoded:
Briefing: The automotive industry raised a collective eyebrow a few years back when Mazda announced that it would sell a two-row version of its excellent three-row CX-90 , but as a new model under the new name of CX-70 , and for good reason.

The automotive industry raised a collective eyebrow a few years back when Mazda announced that it would sell a two-row version of its excellent three-row CX-90 , but as a new model under the new name of CX-70 , and for good reason. When we first saw the CX-70 in early 2024 , we called it out as "literally just a CX-90 with only two rows of seats and a different name," because that's what it was, despite Mazda insisting it was a new model. Now, after just two model years, it seems that Mazda has finally come to its senses, as it announced October 27 that it's canceling the CX-70, and replacing it with a two-row CX-90 that will sell alongside the three-row CX-90 for 2027. We're sure all five members of the CX-70 fan club are devastated by this decision, but we're also sure they'll get over it.

The 2027 Mazda CX-90 two-row drops the CX-70's plug-in hybrid option , so it will only be offered with the turbocharged 3.3-liter inline six-cylinder engine and in 280-horsepower Turbo Premium Sport trim or 340-horsepower Turbo S Premium Sport trim level. The CX-90 three-row continues to be offered with both of those engines as well as a plug-in hybrid power train, and a wider array of trim levels. The cheapest 2027 CX-90 three-row is the 3.3 Turbo Select trim, which starts at $41,345, and the cheapest 2027 CX-90 two-row is 3.3 Turbo Premium Sport trim which starts at $1,200 less than its three-row equivalent at $48,525. (All prices include $1,645 destination.)

If you’re nearing the end of your vehicle’s lease and unsure about your personal transportation plans after the lease is over, then a car lease buyout may be an option worth considering. Provided you really like the car you’re leasing and aren’t quite yet ready to return it.

Perhaps the car is in excellent condition and doesn’t require significant maintenance or repair services. Or maybe you’ve grown accustomed to its reliability and need long-term transportation. Alternatively, a lease buyout might make financial sense if the car’s residual value is less than the market value. The Villa Vie Odyssey announced on Wednesday that it has suspended operations amid rising fuel costs, stranding the ship's passengers in Cambodia. The cruise ship departed Belfast, Northern Ireland, in 2024 to embark on a perpetual around-the-world cruise that has now abruptly ended after two years at sea.

The Villa Vie Odyssey wasn't immune to the U.S. war against Iran, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and the resulting spike in fuel prices. The ship's operator, Villa Vie Residences, said the ship's monthly fuel costs have jumped to $8,000 per cabin in parts of Asia. That's a staggering increase, especially since the ship has 485 cabins and the average monthly fuel cost was previously $1,800 per cabin. The Villa Vie Odyssey tried to cut fuel use by spending more time in port. The operator even floated the idea of adding a fuel surcharge, but admitted it couldn't realistically pass the full increase on to passengers.
